persona: Field biologist running a breeding-bird point-count survey comparing forest and meadow sites over one field season
source_style: typed by hand into Excel each evening after transcribing paper field data sheets from the point counts

columns.name: Date
columns.notes: survey date, 4 visits biweekly through the breeding season, stored as an Excel date

columns.name: Site
columns.notes: 4 site codes: FOR-1, FOR-2 (forest), MDW-1, MDW-2 (meadow)

columns.name: Habitat
columns.notes: 'forest' or 'meadow', redundant with the Site prefix but kept as its own column for easy filtering

columns.name: Observer
columns.notes: observer initials; KP always covers the forest sites, JL always covers the meadow sites

columns.name: Species
columns.notes: common name; not every species in the habitat's pool is detected on every visit

columns.name: Count
columns.notes: number of individuals of that species detected on that visit; flocking species (Red-winged Blackbird, Eastern Meadowlark) can run higher

columns.name: Temp_C
columns.notes: air temperature at the start of that site-visit, one value repeated across every species row of the same visit

columns.name: Wind_Beaufort
columns.notes: Beaufort wind scale 0-3, one value per visit, repeated across its species rows

columns.name: Time_start
columns.notes: 24-hour clock HH:MM, start time of that point count

columns.name: Notes
columns.notes: free text, blank for ~92% of rows

clean_table.generation_rule: Long/stacked format: one row per (site, date, detected species). 4 sites (FOR-1, FOR-2 = forest; MDW-1, MDW-2 = meadow) x 4 dates (2024-05-04, 2024-05-18, 2024-06-01, 2024-06-15) = 16 site-visits, iterated date-major then site-major in that fixed order. Each visit draws k=rng.randint(3,5) species without replacement (rng.sample) from a 5-species habitat pool (forest: American Robin, Yellow Warbler, Eastern Wood-Pewee, Red-eyed Vireo, Black-capped Chickadee; meadow: Song Sparrow, Red-winged Blackbird, Common Yellowthroat, Eastern Meadowlark, American Robin), in the order rng.sample returns them (not alphabetized). Count = rng.randint(1,4), plus rng.randint(0,3) extra if the species is Red-winged Blackbird or Eastern Meadowlark. Distance_band drawn with rng.choices weighted [0.35,0.30,0.20,0.15] over [0-25m,25-50m,50-100m,>100m]. Temp_C = round(10.0 + date_idx*2.5 + rng.uniform(-1,1), 1) (warms over the season, date_idx 0-3), same value for every species row of that visit. Wind_Beaufort = rng.randint(0,3), same per visit. Time_start built from start_minutes = 370 + site_idx*25 + date_idx*3 (site_idx 0-3 in the SITES list order above, date_idx 0-3), formatted HH:MM. Notes is one of ['singing male','flyover, not on point','pair observed','heard only'] with probability 0.08 per row (rng.random()<0.08), else blank. All randomness from a single random.Random(42), consumed in the exact call order: k, species sample, temp jitter, wind, then per species: count, extra-count (if flocking), distance, note-roll, note-choice (if triggered) -- looping site-major within each date, date outer loop.

intended_analysis: Does breeding-bird species richness and total abundance differ between forest and meadow point-count sites, and does detection change across the breeding season (biweekly visits)? A mixed model or repeated-measures comparison would treat site as the sampling unit with repeated visits.
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Treating each row as an independent bird survey rather than recognizing that Temp_C, Wind_Beaufort, Site, Habitat, and Observer are repeated within a single site-visit (only Species/Count/Distance_band/Notes vary row to row); and missing that absence of a species-date-site combination means 'not detected', not a missing value to impute.
